disease: Long QT syndrome type 3 (LQT3; SCN5A gain-of-function, late sodium current)

emergence.disease: Long QT syndrome type 3 (LQT3; SCN5A gain-of-function, late sodium current)
emergence.summary: Long QT syndrome type 3 (LQT3) is the cardiac-sodium-channel form of congenital long QT syndrome, caused by GAIN-of-function mutations in SCN5A, which encodes the alpha-subunit of the cardiac voltage-gated sodium channel NaV1.5 (chr3p22.2). NaV1.5 normally opens to drive the rapid upstroke of the ventricular action potential and then INACTIVATES; LQT3 GOF alleles impair inactivation (the deltaKPQ in-frame deletion is the classic example) and leave a small persistent LATE sodium current (late INa) flowing during the plateau. That extra inward depolarising charge PROLONGS the action-potential duration and the QT interval, predisposing to torsades de pointes and sudden cardiac death (events characteristically at rest / during sleep). The kit reads this as the cardiac late-sodium-current / repolarisation axis driven UP (channel GOF -> the gate fails to stay in the OFF / inactivated basin -> a runaway persistent current), the action-potential-prolonging drive OVER-shooting. This is the kit's FIRST cardiac ION-CHANNEL axis (distinct from hypertrophic cardiomyopathy's MECHANICAL / contractile cardiac axis) and its FIRST channel GAIN-of-function read: where the two prior channel reads are LOSS-of-function channels restored by POTENTIATION (CFTR in cystic fibrosis; the K_ATP / SUR1-Kir6.2 channel in congenital hyperinsulinism, both axis DOWN -> potentiate), LQT3 is a channel whose EXCESS current must be RESTRAINED (axis UP -> restrain) -- a NEW channel-lever class, the channel analogue of the gain-of-toxicity reads (HCM hypercontractility, Wilson copper). Correction is to RESTRAIN the late sodium current: mexiletine, an approved late-INa-blocking class-IB antiarrhythmic, is the GENE-SPECIFIC therapy for LQT3 -- it preferentially blocks the persistent late current, shortens the QT interval and reduces life-threatening arrhythmic events, and the emerged switch independently re-derives it (Mazzanti 2016 JACC). IMPORTANT HONESTY: the response is GENOTYPE-DEPENDENT -- some SCN5A alleles are mexiletine-SENSITIVE and others mexiletine-INSENSITIVE (the biophysics of the specific inactivation defect determine sensitivity), so the corrective DIRECTION (block the excess late INa) is forced [F] while the realised QTc-shortening MAGNITUDE is [O]; an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator remains the mainstay for high-risk patients (not a switch lever). beta-blockers (nadolol / propranolol), the first-line therapy for LQTS OVERALL, are recorded here as a DOWNSTREAM NON-lever on this switch axis: they act by an anti-adrenergic mechanism rather than blocking the late current, are less effective in LQT3 than in LQT1 / LQT2, and can even be pro-arrhythmic in LQT3 by slowing the heart rate -- the Rett / trofinetide downstream-agent discipline. The OTHER major LQTS genes are framed as CONTEXT, deliberately NOT as a convergence: KCNQ1 (LQT1, the slow-delayed-rectifier IKs potassium channel) and KCNH2 / hERG (LQT2, the rapid-delayed-rectifier IKr potassium channel) are LOSS-of-function POTASSIUM channels -- the OPPOSITE channel-level mechanism to SCN5A's gain (a K-current DOWN vs an Na-current UP, both prolonging QT by lowering the net repolarising balance). They CANNOT be folded into one convergent switch read because their channel-level directions are opposite -- a clean demonstration that the kit reads the (gene x mechanism), not the syndrome label, and that the lead therapy is correspondingly GENE-SPECIFIC. The gamma read is of the SCN5A promoter switch STRUCTURE (chr3p22.2); the disease lesions are coding (the deltaKPQ deletion; inactivation-impairing missense alleles), outside the promoter firewall. The same gene's LOSS-of-function alleles cause a DISTINCT disease (Brugada syndrome / conduction disease) -- a different (mechanism) read not conflated here. Magnitude [O].
emergence.emergent_axis: cardiac late sodium current (late INa) through NaV1.5 / ventricular action-potential repolarisation -- the SCN5A channel normally inactivates after the upstroke; GOF alleles leave a persistent late INa during the plateau, extra inward depolarising charge that PROLONGS the action-potential duration and QT interval (the gate over-stays the conducting state -> a runaway late current). The kit's first cardiac ion-channel axis and first channel gain-of-function (axis UP / restrain) read, the channel contrast to the LOF channels restored by potentiation (CFTR, K_ATP)

per_gene.note: SCN5A encodes NaV1.5, the pore-forming alpha-subunit of the cardiac voltage-gated sodium channel that drives the action-potential upstroke and then inactivates. LQT3 GAIN-of-function alleles impair inactivation, leaving a persistent LATE sodium current (late INa) during the plateau that prolongs repolarisation (the deltaKPQ deletion is the classic example). chr3p22.2. NCBI official symbol SCN5A. LQT3 = OMIM 603830. Coding lesions; promoter firewall respected.

treatment_A_switch.disease: Long QT syndrome type 3 (LQT3; SCN5A gain-of-function, late sodium current)

levers.push_direction: block the persistent late sodium current (late INa) through the GOF NaV1.5 channel -> shorten the action-potential plateau / QT toward normal (bring the over-shooting late-current axis DOWN)
levers.agent_class: late-INa-blocking class-IB antiarrhythmic (mexiletine) -- the gene-specific LQT3 therapy
levers.mechanism_grade: [O] QTc-shortening / late-INa-block MAGNITUDE not sequence-derived; GENOTYPE-DEPENDENT -- some SCN5A alleles are mexiletine-SENSITIVE, others mexiletine-INSENSITIVE depending on the biophysics of the inactivation defect, held [O]; the corrective DIRECTION (reduce the excess late INa) is nonetheless forced [F]. An ICD remains the mainstay for high-risk patients (not a switch lever).
levers.src: Mazzanti 2016 J Am Coll Cardiol 67:1053 (mexiletine shortens QTc and reduces arrhythmic events in LQT3); Ruan 2007 Circulation 116:1137 (mutation-specific mexiletine response). Mexiletine is an approved antiarrhythmic; LQT3 use is gene-specific

levers.mechanism_grade: [O] magnitude not derived; ranolazine / lidocaine block late INa but are not LQT3-labelled, held [O]; direction [F]

falsifiers.claim: SCN5A GOF moves the cardiac late-INa / repolarisation axis UP (a persistent late current prolongs the action potential)
falsifiers.falsifier: an LQT3 SCN5A allele that DECREASED the late sodium current / SHORTENED the action-potential duration would refute the channel-on (axis UP) read
falsifiers.measurable_by: late INa (patch clamp) + action-potential duration in SCN5A-mutant cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CM; heterologous expression)

falsifiers.claim: RESTRAINING the late sodium current (mexiletine) is the CORRECTIVE direction
falsifiers.falsifier: if a late-INa blocker LENGTHENED the QT / action-potential duration in late-INa-driven LQT3, the restrain lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: action-potential-duration / QTc response to a late-INa blocker in LQT3 cardiomyocytes or patients
